title: Constructive logic
summary: Constructive logic treats a proof as information and does not accept every classical principle without a construction.

context.note: This node belongs to one explicit foundational presentation; alternate foundations may encode it differently.

assumptions.text: The declared intuitionistic and constructive logics context is fixed.

content.plain: Constructive logic treats a proof as information and does not accept every classical principle without a construction.
content.exact: In intuitionistic natural deduction, P∨¬P is not a theorem for arbitrary P; an existence proof normally carries a witness or method yielding one.
content.example: To prove ∃n P(n), one commonly gives n together with a proof of P(n).
content.caveat: Constructive logic has several formulations and should not be reduced to one slogan.
